identity: Generic hidden PowerShell TCP command dispatchers; no supported family attribution
judgment: The executable wrappers launch hidden, unauthenticated, unrestricted TCP read/evaluate/reply loops. Reserved documentation addresses support an example/test hypothesis, but no package, test harness, consent mechanism, or deployment provenance accompanies these autonomous launchers. On a machine, the balance favors likely malicious remote-command payloads. Runtime connection success and operator identity are unknown.
control_flow: WSH JScript creates WScript.Shell using ActiveXObject and calls Run with window style 0 and wait=false. VBScript uses CreateObject and the same flags. Batch disables echo and launches PowerShell directly.
All launch powershell.exe -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -EncodedCommand. The command is Base64 of UTF-16LE source; both codec layers were decoded without executing the payload.

JScript/batch use [Net.Sockets.TcpClient]::new with 198.51.100.19:8443. VBScript uses New-Object System.Net.Sockets.TCPClient with 192.0.2.42:4444. These are documentation addresses, not corroborated infrastructure.
GetStream obtains the TCP network stream. A zero-filled 65536-byte buffer receives each Read. The nonzero-byte-count loop decodes exactly the received bytes using UTF8.GetString.

The decoded command is evaluated with iex or Invoke-Expression, stderr is merged into stdout, and Out-String collects output. UTF8.GetBytes encodes that output, Write sends it to the same stream, and Flush forces buffered output.

Read returning zero exits the loop and Close closes the client. There is no authentication, allowlist, TLS, reconnect, framing, persistence, privilege escalation, file staging, deletion, or defender modification in these bytes. Close is transport cleanup, not artifact removal. No child-shell I/O bridge is created.
coverage_changes: Added notable UTF-8 GetString decoding; extended existing UTF-8 GetBytes observation to batch decoded text.
Promoted the existing encoded-buffer Read observation to a plaintext-or-decoded text matcher and renamed it. Its regex and original file/platform scope are retained.

Added suspicious delimiter-bounded GetString-before-evaluator syntax and required it plus the buffer Read for the existing TCP dispatcher. A TCP connection plus an independent local expression previously caused an unsupported hostile remote-command claim. Existing plaintext, batch, and encoded attack fixtures retain their hostile findings.
Moved PowerShell option/operator-prefix syntax from shell creation to process arguments, preserving matcher, scope, severity, and exact consumers.

Consolidated generic Run zero/Boolean arguments under existing neutral dispatch observations. Arbitrary objects with Run methods do not establish WSH process creation or hidden windows. Updated consumers and focused expectations; wait=true remains accurately observable as a Boolean argument.

Consolidated the narrower PowerShell WindowStyle Hidden command observation into the existing hidden-command observation. All valid command matches and type scope are retained; misleading matches inside non-PowerShell words are not preserved. Consumers reference the canonical trait. Explicitly negated documentation is excluded by the canonical matcher; it does not establish a hidden launch.
Extended the NoProfile observation to JavaScript and VBScript launch command text. Severity stays notable.

Moved lexical command/result field-or-assignment separators from data serialization to source syntax metadata, preserving both matchers, proximity, severities, and the sole explicit composite consumer. Variable names and separators do not establish serialization.
Removed T1105 from the PowerShell dispatch file default: these matchers establish evaluation/tasking, not ingress file transfer.
distinct_hostile_behavior_limit: Remote task execution and hidden invocation are evidenced. The three retained hostile findings include plaintext/decoded and encoded tasking representations; additional independent attacker objectives are not supported. No duplicate hostile rules were added to raise the score.

consumer_review.wsh_suite: Existing check.py has eight baseline failures involving unrelated startup flow overclaims and stale script-run-method-call expectations. An original HEAD rules snapshot reproduces the same eight failures. No suspicious/hostile findings changed across any WSH control; the intentional generic Run wait=true observation is neutral. Details are in scratch/wsh-controls.before.json, wsh-controls.json, and wsh-preexisting-failures.json.

limitations: Static source analysis only; payloads were not executed or contacted.
atomscan notes that the installed v18 model has an older feature specification than the analyzer expects. It still flags all three; there is no remaining verdict disagreement.
No archive members. JScript and VBScript have separately analyzed decoded PowerShell children; batch exposes decoded text without a separate child report.

Precision audit: plaintext dispatcher 6.7, encoded dispatcher 4.4, hidden encoded tasking 5.9. The plaintext dispatcher is inherited from the PowerShell child in JScript, rather than matching its JavaScript file type directly.
